text:
Situation: DOBUTamine hydrochloride has been on the FDA shortage list since 2017-11-06 and remains Current as of 2026-10-21. The listing includes Baxter Healthcare, Hainan Poly Pharm. Co., Ltd., and Hospira, Inc. as affected companies. Our Corvale East and Corvale General inventory carries Baxter Healthcare Corporation labels with NDC 0338-1073-02. A Baxter Healthcare Corporation plant (FEI 1416980) was inspected on 2026-04-02 and classified OAI. Corvale East holds 16 bags of 100 mg/100 mL (250 mL) for 3.1 days and 9 vials of 12.5 mg/mL (20 mL) for 1.7 days. Corvale General holds 153 bags of 100 mg/100 mL (250 mL) for 25 days, 135 bags of 400 mg/100 mL for 23.4 days, and 82 vials of 12.5 mg/mL for 14 days. Corvale Lakeside holds 17 bags of 100 mg/100 mL (250 mL) for 13.6 days.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the dobutamine hydrochloride shortage on 2017-11-06 and it remains Current as of 2026-10-21. The shortage listing includes Baxter Healthcare, Hainan Poly Pharm. Co., Ltd., and Hospira, Inc. as affected companies.

Our position: Corvale East is critically low on the 100 mg/100 mL, 250 mL bag and the 12.5 mg/mL, 20 mL vial. Corvale General has sufficient supply of the 100 mg/100 mL, 250 mL bag to support a transfer while retaining two weeks of stock. Alternate suppliers are not on the FDA shortage list but their labels do not identify a manufacturing plant. An alternate concentration from Hospira, Inc. is available but requires dose recalculation and pharmacist verification.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 57 bags of DOBUTamine hydrochloride 100 mg/100 mL, 250 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East. Approval required: Pharmacy Director.
2. Evaluate purchase from HF Acquisition Co LLC, DBA HealthFirst if transfer does not resolve the gap. Approval required: Buyer.
3. Evaluate purchase from Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. if needed. Approval required: Buyer.
4. Use DOBUTamine 12.5 mg/mL from Hospira, Inc. as an alternate concentration with pharmacist verification of dose and volume. Approval required: Pharmacist.

Not recommended: No clinical dosing changes or protocol modifications; those are for the treating clinicians and the committee.
